citation_convention: Numbers cite (file, lens/id, field). Unless noted, Phase C numbers are the skeptic_numbers of that observation in analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json. All 15 proposals' citations were checked programmatically: every cited (lens,id) is in _index.json exactly once with reproduced == true. Counts quoted without a CI have none in the committed source; no rate was derived by this ranker.
standing_caveats: INTERPRETATION, not data: everything in why_this_rank, build_first and relation_to_phase_b.

Phase C lenses read the B split before Phase B ran; every Phase C number here is in-sample on B (or the full population), not held out. The proposals (commit a6317dd) predate the Phase B results (commit db886ab).

Novelty is UNVERIFIED for every item; none is asserted to be new.

ranking.name: Provider-minted request-id clock: per-stream skew bracket and response binding (inter-request ceiling and aiv_cu provider-header windows kept only as unmeasured extensions)
merged_from: power#1 Server-minted id bracket and binding test
robustness#1 Provider-clock ceiling on each tool round
coverage#1 Server-minted request-id bracket as a stretch guard for latency checks
coverage#4 Provider-clock action windows for logs without per-call stamps (AI Village computer use)
ranking.observation: Anthropic request ids decode as UUIDv7: swechat 154,815/154,815 v7|var2 against 2,418.98 expected by chance (n silently includes 50 Vertex ids the loader stored as message ids), cc_local 31,085/31,085 (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O1). Decoded server time agrees with client stamps in 155,067/155,267 = 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992] counting every copy; holdout A 11,047 ids, 0 violations (O2). One constant skew per stream places every id between the stream's last input event and first output block in all but 10 of 3,674 swechat CC streams, rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466] session-clustered (tolerance 0 s gives 18, 5 s gives 7); cc_local 1 of 847; slack U-L p5 1,102 / p50 2,268 / p95 3,807 ms (O5). Placebo on 3,673 swechat streams (counts, no CI in source): moving one response's first event 5 s earlier flags 1,441, 30 s earlier flags 3,581; moving it 5/30/300 s later flags 10, the baseline; rolling every id by one response flags 3,667 (O5). aiv_cc stores 0 request ids (O13). aiv_cu: Anthropic msg ids carry time only from 2026-07-06 (O4); bracket streams opus/sonnet/haiku/fable 105/80/27/32 and Gemini 255/92 all 0, OpenAI 3/463 (O5), but row-insert lag (median 5.7-12 s) makes the aiv_cu test weak by construction (O3 skeptic_problem). Gemini server-timing fits the DB row gap 0/12,292, slack min 563.8 ms, 347 of 2,000 B sessions (two_clocks/O7); every aiv_cu call has lat == 0, 59,956/59,956 (correlations/O4).
ranking.test_measurement: Tolerance and decoder fixed on split A; test on B, holdout A and cc_local; report per tamper type (never pooled) with session-clustered CIs against the honest 10/3,674 (swechat CC) and 1/847 (cc_local). (1) Single-response tampers, none yet measured: splice one response with its id from another session or from later in the same session; swap two adjacent responses' ids; delay one tool result by D in {1, 2, 5, 30, 300} s with every id untouched, and the consistent variant that shifts that result and all later client events by D; insert a fabricated tool_result stamped after the consuming request's id time. (2) Refine the back-date curve on a 1-30 s grid and report D at power 0.5 and 0.9 next to U-L p50 2,268 ms. (3) Only then the ceiling: S = t_req(k+1) - t_req(k) against client timers, reporting the honest slack distribution (S-D)/S before any power claim. (4) aiv_cu Gemini header variant: w = created_at - HTTP Date with positive controls (pause, explicit sleep) before any long-vs-trivial separability claim. Kill rule: if single-response splice/delay power at the honest rate does not exceed the measured 5 s back-date point (1,441/3,673), report that and stop the line.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: 10/3,674 swechat streams inconsistent at 2 s tolerance (18 at 0 s, 7 at 5 s) and 1/847 cc_local (O5); resume/fork copies re-stamped onto 1-2 timestamps (178 request ids in 2 session pairs, O7) must be deduped, and 12 far offsets remain unexplained after dedupe (O2); within-stream clock steps (drift above 2 s in 15 swechat sessions and 2 of 18 cc_local sessions, O6 skeptic) are not absorbed by a constant skew; 1 s resolution of OpenAI/Gemini ids and HTTP Date (O3, distributions/D19); aiv_cu OpenAI 3/463 inconsistent; 329 v2.1 gap-0 call/result pairs with no explanation (two_clocks/O12 skeptic). Blind spots by construction, not false positives: late-stamping (later shifts flag only the baseline 10), in-band fabrication by the model (the harness stamps it consistently), content substitution, and any editor who re-mints ids (unsigned; the layout was inferred from data, so a forger can infer it too).
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - do not claim novel; prior art not checked. Time extraction from UUIDv1/v7/ULID/Snowflake ids and skew bracketing are standard; the bounding logic matches event-time bounding in the Gladyshev & Patel line (the grounding skeptic's own unverified recollection, analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json). The possibly new part is narrow: provider-minted LLM request ids as the bound on agent tool-log stamps and as a response-binding test.
ranking.why_this_rank: INTERPRETATION. (a) It is the only merged proposal with a measured tamper response on honest data: at an honest stream rate of 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466], back-dating one response by 5 s flags 1,441/3,673 streams and by 30 s 3,581/3,673 (O5). The other merged proposals report honest rates plus arithmetic predictions for their new witness; the one other measured curve, which rank 5 inherits from token_conservation/TC2, belongs to Phase A's own conservation plan and needs 8,913 inserted chars for power 0.5 in swechat CC. (b) The value is minted by the provider on request receipt and is never written by the model, but it is unsigned and re-mintable by an informed log editor, so it binds post-hoc retiming and misbinding only, one-sided (back-dating, not late-stamping), at per-turn resolution (U-L p50 2,268 ms). That the model never sees the id is reasoning, not an observation. (c) Two of five scaffold families: swechat CC 3,674 streams and cc_local 847; aiv_cu weak by construction; aiv_cc, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI have no server-minted clock. (d) Bracket code and placebo already exist. Penalties applied from analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json: 'the only invariant with a measured tamper-power curve' is false (TC2 has one); '3,667 misbinding' is an every-response roll, not a single splice; 'in-band fabrication cannot produce a consistent one' is wrong; the robustness ceiling (S vs client timers) and the coverage 'delay a result' evasion were never run; '178/178' is implied by the offsets. These shrink its scope to post-hoc retiming, but the reproduced core (O5) stands, and on criterion (a) nothing else is close.

ranking.name: Execution-window consistency of clock evidence printed by generator commands (git commit_date of resolved SHAs; fresh time readings); harness-timer legs dropped as internal redundancy
merged_from: power#3 Execution-window consistency: time evidence in or around a result must fit the window
robustness#3 Nested timer chain: printed durations <= model-invisible harness timers <= provider interval
ranking.observation: Commit SHAs printed in swechat CC Bash results resolve for 3,936 claims in 1,491 sessions, and commit_date lies in [call ts - 2 s, result ts + 2 s] for 3,917 = 0.995 [0.992, 0.998], median offset -0.103 s [-0.137, -0.062] (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json commit_witness/O9). Of the 19 out-of-window claims, 15 are cat/tail/head/grep re-reads of earlier output files, 1 is an amend with an explicit GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, 3 are unexplained (O11). 2,198/6,141 = 0.358 [0.321, 0.394] of commit claims do not resolve (O10), so non-resolution alone is not a signal. Fresh epochs in collusion-wiki prose: with a fractional part 0/459 postdate the save, Wilson upper 0.0083, a POST-HOC split (ext_witness/O10). Codex model-visible Wall time never exceeds the call-to-output gap on exec_command, 0 of 4,408, while 0.1 s-display shell_command headers exceed it in 646/1,817 by at most 49 ms (two_clocks/O6). Dropped per the grounding skeptic as same-clock redundancy: bash_progress floor rule 0/112,677 (two_clocks/O9) and harness timers inside the window (O8); the progress stream is absent from current Claude Code, 0 of 332 cc_local main files (raw_census/A6-O10).
ranking.test_measurement: swechat CC B transcripts plus the Entire commit table. (1) Fix the generator vs re-reader command list on split A (not from the 19 B cases), apply it to B and report the honest out-of-window rate per command class with session-clustered CIs. (2) Tamper: replay a real commit-bearing output into a later call of the same session and into another session of the same repo; shift a commit call's stamps on a delta grid; report power vs delta at the honest rate. (3) Measure the share of all tool results carrying a resolvable SHA or a fresh generator-printed clock reading; stop rule: if that share is too small to matter, report it and stop. (4) Printed-duration leg (pytest 'in X s', go test, shell 'real') only after (3), with regexes pre-registered on A and re-readers excluded.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: re-reads of saved output (15/19), an explicit committer date (1/19), 3 of 3,936 unexplained (commit_witness/O11); auto-backgrounded commands whose result window is not the execution window (111 of 188 swechat 120 s shell results, outliers/O9); same-timestamp blocks and 329 unexplained v2.1 gap-0 pairs where any zero-width window check would fire (two_clocks/O12); display rounding (646/1,817 shell_command headers, two_clocks/O6); stored ids echoed by tools are not fresh (440 of 561 v7 mentions more than 10 min older, ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O14); sandbox clock offset (median -1 s, ext_witness/O10). Unresolved SHAs (0.358 of honest claims) must abstain, not fire.
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - do not claim novel. The git leg is a claim-vs-record existence check overlapping our own git shadow-state core plan, and the window logic is event-time bounding (Gladyshev & Patel line, listed) per analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json. Bounding non-recomputable outputs by the log's own clock differs from METR-style recomputation, but may be described elsewhere; not checked.
ranking.why_this_rank: INTERPRETATION. (a) Honest in-window 0.995 [0.992, 0.998] (19 of 3,936 out) at about 2 s resolution, comparable to ranks 3-5, but no tamper power is measured, and the re-read exclusion that would cut the 19 to 4 was read off the same data. (b) The strongest witness of the five: commit_date is hashed into a SHA held in an external repo, a fabricator cannot print a resolving SHA without a real commit, and a lying backend that replays a real commit output lands outside the window. Grounding correction applied: committer dates can be set (O11 amend), so the cost is getting a commit with a chosen date into the external repo, not making it at that time. (c) Narrow: Entire-linked swechat CC only (3,936 resolved claims, 1,491 sessions); the share of results carrying such evidence is unmeasured; cc_local has no commit table. (d) Moderate; the commit join exists. It ranks second because it is the only proposal that ties tool-result content to an external, content-addressed record; it ranks below 1 because no tamper response is measured. Penalized for bundling same-clock harness timers as evidence, the overstated git evasion cost, and the post-hoc ext_witness split.

ranking.name: Quantized provider image-token ledger as a screenshot-count witness for GUI agents
merged_from: power#4 Quantized server-usage ledger of result modality
coverage#5 Image-token quanta as a screenshot-count witness for GUI agents
robustness#5 Provider quantization lattices (image-unit part only; usage_in modes (D7) and the reasoning lattice (D1) dropped per skeptic; Codex 128 rule kept only as a plausibility check)
ranking.observation: aiv_cu Gemini prompt IMAGE tokens change by 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11,668/11,668 consecutive pairs (258 for gemini-2.5-pro, n 4,925; 1,064 for 3-pro 682, 3.1-pro 3,166, 3.5-flash 2,895), never negative; the increment is positive in 5,059/5,092 GUI windows and 0 in shell 0/4,134, get_pixel_coords 0/2,033 and pause 0/202 windows (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json token_conservation/TC9). Pro rows sit on {258, 1064, 2160} in 10,569/10,569 and no session mixes lattices, 0/309 (distributions/D3). Untested above 40 images while 442 population sessions exceed 40 GUI turns; gemini-3.8-flash (277 pairs) never shows an image (TC9). Gemini rows cover 347 of 2,000 aiv_cu B sessions (two_clocks/O7). aiv_cc (one agent): residual per stripped image median 890.1 [887.9, 890.9] over 4,543 pairs in 64 runs, but 227 fall in the 316-562 bin, below the honest per-turn |residual| p99 of 690.2, which itself ranges 651-735 by split (aiv_accounting/O11, O10). Codex cached tokens are multiples of 128 in 16,106/16,106 calls, found post hoc (swechat_tables/T11).
ranking.test_measurement: aiv_cu Gemini: fix rules on split A, test on B. Predict image units per window from logged action types and require dIMAGE = units x per-model constant. Tamper honest B windows: delete one GUI result, relabel a GUI action as shell, insert a fabricated GUI call and result, splice in a window from another session; report detection per direction at the honest rates (33/5,092 GUI misses; 0 increments in non-GUI windows), and state a session-level honest false-positive rate, which no file states yet. Run the above-40-image population regime before any claim past 40. aiv_cc one-image add/remove at FPR 1% as a one-agent case study only. Secondary: narrated on-screen facts in windows with zero image increment.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5,092 GUI windows with no increment, unexplained and not cap effects (images before: median 4, max 31; TC9); units depend on model generation (258, 1,064, 2,160; D3); cached IMAGE counts are off-lattice (11/3,022 and 40/9,318; D3), so only prompt-side counts are usable; pruning beyond 40 images untested; aiv_cc unlogged context resets, 30 in 12 runs, 27 of them image pairs (aiv_accounting/O12); user-pasted images vary in size (swechat CC single-image residual p5-p95 121-1,618; TC17); per-window misses compound at session level, unmeasured.
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - do not claim novel. Token-count plausibility checks are familiar in billing; neither grounding check found overlap with a listed prior-art item. Using a provider's per-modality counts as an exact ledger of how many image-returning results a GUI log may contain may not be described; not checked.
ranking.why_this_rank: INTERPRETATION. (a) The cleanest honest separation in the set: an exact lattice (11,668/11,668), no increment in any shell, get_pixel_coords or pause window, 33/5,092 GUI misses, at one-image resolution; but no tamper response is measured. (b) Written by the provider and not in the model's context (reasoning, not observed); a log editor who knows the unit can recompute it, though one added or removed image must be propagated through every later row; a live forger returning a fake screenshot gets a real increment, so it never speaks to image content. (c) One family: aiv_cu Gemini (347 of 2,000 B sessions) plus one aiv_cc agent. Its value is that it covers the corpus where Probe 1 is NOT_TESTABLE (59,956/59,956 shared stamps) and the Probe 3 tail is DEAD. (d) Cheap; fields are already parsed. Below rank 2 on (b) and (c); above 4-5 because its identity is server-written rather than same-writer or a recount, and it overlaps no listed prior art. Penalized: aiv_cc single-image power is below 1 and unmeasured; the 128 rule is post hoc and trivially satisfied by an informed forger; D7 is a mode, not a lattice, and D1 is on-lattice in 140/6,910 rows, so both are excluded.

ranking.name: Harness structured copy vs model-visible text recount (Claude Code toolUseResult counters)
merged_from: power#2 Visible-text vs harness structured-copy recount at 1-unit resolution
coverage#3 Dual-rendering check: harness-only structured result fields vs the model-visible result text
ranking.observation: Read toolUseResult.file.numLines equals the numbered lines of the visible result in 87,827/88,229 = 0.9954 [0.9950, 0.9959] (cluster [0.9947, 0.9960], 4,603 files); all 402 mismatches are named formats: 282 persisted-output previews, 105 offset warnings, 7 identical-to references, 7 redactions, 1 negative line numbers. cc_local main 570/578, all 8 empty-file warnings; cc_local subagent files carry numLines in 0 of 12 Read results (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json raw_census/A6-O1). Agent/Task totalToolUseCount equals the distinct nested tool_use ids in 6,623/6,623, Wilson [0.9994, 1.0], with 2,150/8,773 = 0.245 [0.236, 0.254] uncheckable (A6-O2). Field fill: Read 88,229/90,763 = 0.972, Edit structuredPatch 70,553/73,460 = 0.960, Grep 29,535/34,208 = 0.863; Glob totalMatches 0/6,422 in swechat; cc_local Read 578/650 = 0.889 (A6-O4). No progress entries in cc_local, 0 of 332 main files (A6-O10), so the subagent-count leg has no current-CC coverage.
ranking.test_measurement: Freeze the whitelist (the five swechat formats plus the cc_local empty-file warning) and measure the honest unexplained rate on data it was not derived from: split-A swechat files and cc_local sessions after the analysis date. Tamper clean B Read results: add or delete 1/2/5 lines, splice a same-path result from another session, count-preserving substitution, and rewriting a result into a whitelisted format (the whitelist-as-evasion route). Then measure agreement, not fill, for Grep numLines and for Edit structuredPatch line counts against the call's old_string/new_string.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: 402 swechat format mismatches and 8 cc_local empty-file warnings (a detector without the whitelist fires on all of them); the whitelist exempts any result an editor rewrites into those formats; version drift (cc_local subagent 0/12 numLines; Glob totalMatches 0/6,422 swechat vs 1,231/1,234 cc_local); 2,150/8,773 Agent results uncheckable and to be counted as abstentions, not passes; dataset redaction.
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED - probably not novel as a technique. Consistency between redundant fields is a generic integrity idea; the coverage grounding check found substantial overlap with output-grammar parsing (jc), recomputation (METR) and our own filesystem shadow-state plan for the cross-call part (analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json).
ranking.why_this_rank: INTERPRETATION. (a) Honest mismatches 402/88,229, all explained, at 1-line resolution; but '0 unexplained' is in-sample, because the whitelist was built from those same mismatches, and no tamper response is measured. (b) The weakest witness of the five: one harness writes both fields from the same read, so any schema-aware editor rewrites both, count-preserving substitution is invisible, and a lying execution layer yields consistent renderings. (c) The largest call counts (Read fill 0.972 in CC formats), but effectively Claude Code only; the Codex Wall-time pair rests on 5 sessions. (d) The cheapest to build. Below rank 3 on (b) and on prior-art overlap; above rank 5 because it at least touches result content at 1-line resolution.

ranking.name: Commit-time usage-tally freeze plus provider usage identities (turn-structure ledger)
merged_from: power#5 Frozen usage-ledger reconciliation at tolerance 0
robustness#2 Commit-time freeze points (git-held usage tally and agent_changes, cache-chain amplification)
robustness#4 Prompt-cache state as stopwatch / unchanged-prefix certificate (cache-chain identity only; the stopwatch claim is dropped)
ranking.observation: The Entire CLI's 5-integer usage tally equals a tolerance-0 recount of the stored transcript in 4,794/4,836 = 0.9913 [0.9883, 0.9936] Claude-format sessions (repo-clustered [0.9874, 0.9942]): full 2,772, prefix 1,664, window 358, none 42; prefix snapshots precede the last transcript stamp in 1,664/1,664, a median of 3 messages before the end (analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json swechat_tables/T1). After the join fix, unmatched 33/5,701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] across 4 scaffolds (T3); CLI 0.5.x 15/1,048 = 0.0143 [0.0087, 0.0235] (T4). Skeptic: the tally is a deterministic recount of the transcript's own usage fields; its only independent content is the commit-time snapshot. Cache chain exact in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean swechat CC / cc_local / aiv_cc pairs (TC1); aiv_cc 59,747/59,804, with breaks 49/59,772 at gaps under 300 s and 8/32 at 300 s or more, compaction 0/933 (aiv_accounting/O9). Content edits that leave usage alone need 8,913/10,000 inserted chars for power 0.5/0.9 in swechat CC (token_conservation/TC2); deleting a 100-1,000-char result has power 0.003 (TC16).
ranking.test_measurement: On the 5,701 tallied sessions: delete one assistant message.id; insert a copied message.id; append after the snapshot; insert a tool_use block into an existing message.id; edit result content. Report detection per tamper against the honest 33/5,701, per CLI version. Measure the share of tool results inside a frozen span. Characterize the swechat CC and cc_local cache-chain breaks before any session-level identity flag.
ranking.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5,701 unmatched after the join correction (6 of the 33 in one repo; T4), higher in CLI 0.5.x (0.0143); the dataset join artifact must be fixed first (31 of 64 raw mismatches; T3); checkpoint rows duplicated across forks, 3,650/13,406 rows (T9); honest cache-chain breaks are routine at session level in swechat CC (exact in 0.975 of clean pairs) and uncharacterized there; aiv_cc unlogged resets (30; aiv_accounting/O12) and compaction (0/933 hold); non-null stop_reason responses omitted from result.usage depending on SDK version and date (15/211 runs; aiv_accounting/O7).
ranking.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED, and probably mostly prior art: a commit-time tally acts as a seal (hash-chain sealing: Agent Flight Recorder, NovaFabric, listed); the Entire CLI is installed capture tooling; ledger reconciliation is standard audit practice; content binding is our own Phase A token-conservation plan. The robustness grounding check found the cache-chain amplification adds nothing at tolerance 0 (analysis/out/phase_c/_proposals_grounded.json).
ranking.why_this_rank: INTERPRETATION. (a) Honest unmatched 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] with one-message resolution by arithmetic (unmeasured), but blind to tool-result content: a content edit faces only token conservation (8,913 chars at power 0.5 in swechat CC). (b) The model never sees usage (reasoning), but the tally is a recount an editor can redo, and the anchor is a local git branch, rewritable until pushed; push time is not in the data, and forks as copies outside the forger's control are unmeasured. (c) The frozen anchor exists only in Entire-linked swechat sessions; the identities span five families but constrain turn structure, not results. (d) Low. Last because it is mostly listed prior art, it does not speak to result content, and the grounding checks flagged its 'out-of-band' and 'every API turn' framings as overclaims. Excluded outright from the ranking: the prompt-cache 'stopwatch' (only 8/32 long gaps break the chain, and honest unlogged pruning produces the same signature).

build_first: INTERPRETATION. Build rank 1 first, as its single-response tamper suite on the existing bracket: splice or swap one response's request id, delay one tool result with ids untouched and with a consistent re-stamp, and a 1-30 s back-date grid, on swechat CC B, holdout A and cc_local. Why: (1) it is the only proposal whose new witness has both an honest baseline (10/3,674 = 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466]) and a tamper response (5 s back-date flags 1,441/3,673 streams, 30 s flags 3,581/3,673; analysis/out/phase_c/_index.json ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O5) already measured, so the next run has a defined kill rule: stop if single-response splice/delay power at the honest rate does not beat the 5 s back-date point. (2) The bracket code and placebo exist, so it is the cheapest proposal with a measurable outcome. (3) It covers the same Claude Code corpora where Probe 1 is ALIVE (cc_local) or WEAK (swechat CC), and is the only proposal that can show whether a post-hoc stretch of call-to-result latency, the obvious evasion of Probe 1 for compute-bound tools, gets caught. Limits to state up front: it says nothing about in-band fabrication; it binds only editors who do not re-mint ids, and whether ids can be checked against provider records is untestable with our data. If the goal were instead a witness that binds result content to an external record, rank 2 (git commit_date window) would go first, gated on its coverage-share stop rule.
relation_to_phase_b: INTERPRETATION over committed numbers. Threat model: Probes 1-4 test signals of fabrication by the producer (inline generation, missing friction, knowledge from nowhere, invented values). The Phase C proposals mostly bind post-hoc edits to a log (retiming, inserted/deleted/misbound turns); among the five ranked here, only rank 2 tests a result's content against an external record. Evidence quality: Probes 1-4 were pre-registered (thresholds from split A, commit 3df8d28), produced mechanical verdicts on B, and were independently re-derived in 49 of 50 unit checks, the miss being one overgeneralized sentence in the Probe 1 summary (analysis/out/phase_b_verification.json). The proposals come from lenses that read B before Phase B ran; they are not pre-registered, their honest rates are in-sample, and only rank 1 has a measured tamper response for its new witness (rank 5's content leg reuses token_conservation/TC2). Neither side has a fabricated positive control; Probe 1's G-vs-W AUC is a generation-bound proxy. Tested results (analysis/out/probe_1..4.json): Probe 1 is ALIVE only in opencode (fp 7/4,419 = 0.0016 [0, 0.0033], AUC 0.999 [0.998, 1.000]) and cc_local (1/1,019 = 0.0010 [0, 0.0033], AUC 0.919 [0.881, 0.971]); swechat CC is WEAK (fp 72/20,937 = 0.0034 [0.0025, 0.0044], AUC 0.987, downgraded because the floor is UNSTABLE, 21/156 series); aiv_cc and codex are WEAK (fp 0.075 [0.040, 0.119], 0.062 [0.026, 0.118]); aiv_cu, whowhen and cursor are NOT_TESTABLE. Probe 2 has no ALIVE cell: the best is S_deep 0.144 [0.125, 0.163] in swechat CC main (WEAK), and it is DEAD in codex, opencode and cc_local main threads. Probe 3: the zero-error tail is ALIVE only in swechat CC (Z = 9/413 = 0.022, Wilson [0.012, 0.041]) and DEAD in cc_local (15/36 = 0.417) and aiv_cu (678/988 = 0.686); reaction is at best WEAK. Probe 4: hex is never ALIVE (swechat CC WEAK, 0.110 [0.041, 0.232]; aiv_cu WEAK, 0.093 [0.043, 0.216]; INSUFFICIENT_N in 7 units); round numbers are ALIVE in swechat CC, cc_local and swechat/*, but post-hoc tables show the effect is mostly parameter choice. Comparison: rank 1's honest stream rate (0.00272) is in the range of Probe 1's best fp shares (0.0010-0.0034). Ranks 2-5 report honest rates near 0.005 (rank 2 in-window 0.995; rank 5 unmatched 0.0058), far below Probe 2's 0.144 and below Probe 3's session-level 0.022. That comparison is not like for like: the proposals' low rates belong to structural identities a schema-aware editor can satisfy, while the probes' rates belong to behavioural signals a fabricator has to work to avoid. The proposals complement the probes rather than replace them. Rank 1 can bind the stamps Probe 1 relies on. Rank 3 covers aiv_cu, where Probe 1 is NOT_TESTABLE and the Probe 3 tail is DEAD. Among the ranked proposals, rank 2 is the only one that tests result content against an external record; no Phase B probe does. No proposal revives a DEAD probe cell, and no probe verdict should be read as confirmed by Phase C, because the Phase C lenses read the same B split.
